problems.desc: attempt 2 is the precise definition. A correct response also names what each other attempt leaves out: attempt 1 never says the point lies ON the segment, so a point off the segment could still be the same distance from both ends; attempt 3 says the two pieces look equal rather than that they are congruent, which is not a measurable condition.

a correct counterexample gives two angles whose measures add to 180 but which are not adjacent and do not share a common side lying on a line, for example a 100 degree angle and an 80 degree angle drawn in two separate places, or two right angles in different corners of a page. The response must state both measures (so the hypothesis is met) and say why the pair is not a linear pair (not adjacent, no common ray, non-common sides not opposite rays).

problems.slot: (b) the measure of the whole angle

problems.desc: part (a): a correct repair adds the angle condition -- perpendicular lines intersect to form a right angle, that is an angle of 90 degrees. A response that only says the lines cross, or that they form a square corner without naming a right angle or 90 degrees, has not repaired the definition.

part (a): a correct counterexample gives two congruent angles that are not vertical angles, for example the two base angles of an isosceles triangle, or two separate 40 degree angles drawn side by side. The response must say why they fail the definition of vertical angles: they are not the opposite pair formed by two intersecting lines.

part (b): a correct counterexample names any point off the segment that is the same distance from both endpoints -- any point of the perpendicular bisector other than the midpoint itself. The response must make clear that the point is not on the segment, which is the condition the claim leaves out.

part (a): a correct counterexample describes a point on the segment that is not the midpoint, so the two pieces it creates are not congruent -- for instance a point one quarter of the way along, splitting a 12 unit segment into pieces of 3 and 9.

part (b): a correct rewrite states all three conditions the counterexample exposed -- the point lies on the segment, it lies between the two endpoints, and the two segments it creates are congruent. Wording may vary; all three conditions must be present.
